image_description: A side-profile view of a hammerhead shark swimming in dark water. The shark is oriented horizontally, facing left. Its distinctive cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head) is clearly visible, with eyes at the tips. The body is streamlined with a prominent dorsal fin and visible pectoral fins. The lighting highlights the grey dorsal side and lighter ventral side.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the characteristic T-shaped head structure extending laterally from the body axis.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark spots corresponding to eyes are visible at the very ends of the horizontal head extension.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Resolution is insufficient to definitively locate nostrils on the underside or margin of the cephalofoil from this angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The leading edge of the head appears straight/slightly curved, consistent with typical hammerhead morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The torso tapers smoothly towards the tail, exhibiting the expected hydrodynamic shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Countershading is evident: the top is grey/dark, fading to a lighter/white belly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Image resolution and underwater diffusion prevent visualization of microscopic skin texture (dermal denticles).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large, triangular/falcate dorsal fin is prominent on the upper back.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fin behind the gill slits is visible and matches the broad, triangular description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail fin shows the classic heterocercal structure with a larger upper lobe, though partially faded into the background.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The tail end exhibits significant motion blur or depth-of-field blur, causing a loss of structural definition compared to the head. This is common in aquatic photography but reduces structural clarity.
The transition from grey to white on the belly is extremely smooth and airbrushed, lacking the subtle specular highlights or micro-texture expected on wet skin, suggesting slight over-smoothing.

To verify the continuity of the cephalofoil connection to the body and ensure no floating artifacts or edge bleeding against the dark background.
To assess the realism of the lighting, water diffusion effects, and identify any subtle generative smoothing artifacts.

focus_areas: Cephalofoil structural integrity and connection to the snout
Fin morphology (dorsal and caudal) for anatomical correctness

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'smoothness' of the shark's skin. AI generators often over-smooth wet surfaces. Check if the blur on the tail is natural motion blur or a generative failure to resolve fine details. Verify that the eye placement is strictly at the tips, as AI often drifts them inward.
